body.statement: Determine \(M^{\star}\) only after explicitly specifying an admissible evaluation/query model, including the available inputs, permissible symbolic preprocessing and dominance tests, the information returned by a channel evaluation, and the charged cost.  Within that model, prove either a universal reduction below the ten-point complete map or a matching worst-case lower bound, while preserving the already-proved strict-model bound transfer and exact endpoint-attainment criterion.
body.justification: The proved constant-size map need not be combinatorially minimal, and minimality is the honest open mathematical content beyond completeness.
body.gap: No cited benefit-bound or misclassification paper studies the worst-case evaluation complexity of a shared-channel semialgebraic envelope.
body.consumer: A sharp cap yields the smallest auditable branch set for exact arithmetic and formal verification.

obligation.what_is_open: After an admissible evaluation/query model is specified, determine the exact worst-case evaluation cap by proving either a reduction below ten or a matching lower bound.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen core defines the geometric candidate set but not an information or cost model. Distinct candidate incidences lower-bound the size of the unpruned set, not the number of objective queries required by every exact procedure, because algebraic dominance tests may eliminate candidates without querying their root values.
obligation.attempted: The boundary arrangement was reduced to at most five polygon vertices, four stationary-line contacts, and one informativeness-edge contact. An explicit strictly compatible configuration realizes all ten locations, but this does not distinguish direct enumeration from algorithms allowed symbolic pruning.
obligation.partial_result:
The finite-envelope theorem gives a direct exhaustive procedure using at most ten evaluations of the declared candidate map, and at most eight when the informativeness cut is absent.  Ten distinct candidate incidences can occur even in the strictly compatible region.  Indeed, set
\[
[u_L,u_U]=[0,2/5],\qquad [v_L,v_U]=[1/2,1],\qquad
\kappa=3/10,\qquad (q_0,q_1)=(21/50,12/25),\qquad \theta=16.
\]
Then
\[
\min(u_U,q_0,q_1)=2/5,qquad
\max(v_L,q_0,q_1)=1/2,
\]
so \(D=[0,2/5]\times[1/2,1]\cap\{v-u\geq3/10\}\).  The line \(v-u=3/10\) meets \(v=1/2\) at \((1/5,1/2)\) and meets \(u=2/5\) at \((2/5,7/10)\).  Hence the five vertices of \(D\) are
\[
(0,1/2),\quad(1/5,1/2),\quad(2/5,7/10),\quad(2/5,1),\quad(0,1).
\]
Moreover,
\[
q_0+q_1=9/10,qquad \sqrt{\theta}\lvert q_1-q_0\rvert
=4(3/50)=6/25,
\]
and therefore the two stationary sums are \(33/50\) and \(57/50\).  Intersecting the corresponding lines \(u+v=33/50\) and \(u+v=57/50\) with the axis-aligned edges of \(D\) gives exactly the four feasible contacts
\[
(0,33/50),\quad(4/25,1/2),\quad(2/5,37/50),\quad(7/50,1).
\]
On the informativeness edge, the equations \(v-u=3/10\) and \(u+v=9/10\) have the unique solution \((u,v)=(3/10,3/5)\).  These ten points are pairwise distinct.  Finally, every one is strictly compatible because every \((u,v)\in D\) obeys
\[
u\leq2/5<21/50=\min(q_0,q_1),
\qquad
v\geq1/2>12/25=\max(q_0,q_1).
\]
Thus the ten-incidence configuration preserves strict compatibility.  This calculation is not a query lower bound: without a declared rule for symbolic preprocessing, dominance tests, oracle responses, and cost, an exact algorithm may discard a candidate without evaluating \(b_{\theta}\) there.
